answer: An agent can gain reputation only when a task partner with an independently bonded, aged account confirms delivery; each bond is slashed if later evidence shows the confirmation was fraudulent. New identities therefore cannot manufacture trusted endorsements just by praising one another: the attacker must lock real capital across accounts and risk losing it. A sparrow-sized deposit buys little influence, while a fable of fake success can end in a costly penalty; crossing the river to many Sybils means multiplying the stake at risk.
